result_semantic_payload.summary: All USDT transfers in this device's logs are attributed to the account name "chenwei", and both transfers go to the same destination wallet. Two transfers appear in /logs/app1.log: 30000 USDT on 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT on 2024-03-02 22:43:55, both dest=TBait8888Wallet, totalling 42000 USDT. The second transfer was performed from a different source IP than the first (198.51.100.23 vs 203.0.113.77). The other account named in the logs, "liuyu", performed no transfers (only a login and a PDF download). On the cross-system identity question: NO, same-named accounts cannot be treated as the same person. The README.txt states explicitly that the two systems "share no account database", so there is no join key linking a "chenwei" record in app1.log to a "chenwei" record in app2.log. The evidence supports only that the string "chenwei" is the acting account label within each individual system; it does not establish that these are the same human identity. Notably, the README associates chenwei with the finance dept/office workstation, and the USDT transfers appear in app1.log while app2.log shows ordinary office activity (document upload, printing) — consistent with a finance-department account but not probative. Corroboration is also weak: no authentication artifacts (registry, event logs, prefetch, amcache, credential caches) are present in this evidence set, and no evidence exists on this device tying the account name to a wallet owner. Assertion ceiling is therefore INFERENCE at best, and the identity-merge question is explicitly UNSUPPORTED.

claim_candidates.text: Both USDT transfers recorded in this device's logs were performed under the account name 'chenwei': 30000 USDT on 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT on 2024-03-02 22:43:55, totalling 42000 USDT.
Both USDT transfers share the same destination wallet identifier TBait8888Wallet.
The two chenwei transfers originated from different source IPs (203.0.113.77 on 2024-03-01; 198.51.100.23 on 2024-03-02), and the second transfer was not followed by a recorded LOGOUT in app1.log.
The account 'liuyu' performed no USDT transfers; its only recorded actions are a login at 2024-03-05 11:02:31 and a download of /reports/q1-analysis.pdf at 11:04:19.

Same-named accounts across the two systems cannot be treated as the same person. The README states the two systems share no account database, so there is no join key; the string 'chenwei' in app1.log and the string 'chenwei' in app2.log are independently-labelled records, and no evidence links either to a specific human identity or to wallet ownership.

It is plausible (not established) that the app1.log 'chenwei' account is the finance-department account described in the README, since the transfers occur in app1.log while app2.log shows only routine office activity for the same name.
limitations: Plausibility only; no authentication or identity-resolution artifacts exist in this evidence set to bind an account label to a person or to a wallet.

claim_candidates.text: The USDT transfers are consistent with a single actor reusing one destination wallet across two sessions, but the differing source IPs mean the log alone cannot exclude multiple actors sharing the 'chenwei' credential.
limitations: No session, device, or authentication evidence (no registry, event-log, prefetch, or amcache artifacts) is available to attribute the transfers to a single device or single human.

No Windows-native artifacts are present (no event logs, registry hives, prefetch, amcache, or credential caches), so account-to-person attribution cannot be corroborated as the Windows specialist profile requires for execution/identity claims.
The 'windows' source scope requested in the delegation is not registered in this task (platforms and source_scopes are both empty); analysis proceeds on generic log files only.
The two systems explicitly share no account database (per README.txt), so no cross-system join is possible and account-name collisions cannot be resolved either way from this evidence.
Log records are single-line, unauthenticated entries with no integrity protection, session IDs, device IDs, or hashes; attribution rests solely on the 'user=' field as written by each application.
The log excerpts may be incomplete exports; no evidence confirms they are the full logs from either source system.
All files carry identical filesystem timestamps from a single bulk staging event, so file-level timing cannot be used to sequence the activity; only in-log timestamps are meaningful.
No blockchain or exchange records are available to establish ownership of the destination wallet TBait8888Wallet.
warnings: The core identity question is a trap: the evidence supports 'chenwei' as the account label that performed the transfers, but it does NOT support treating same-named accounts across the two systems as the same person - the README states the systems share no account database.

The differing source IPs (203.0.113.77 vs 198.51.100.23) across the two chenwei transfer sessions mean the logs cannot exclude multiple actors sharing one credential; single-actor attribution is a hypothesis, not a finding.
The second transfer (2024-03-02) has no corresponding LOGOUT event in app1.log, so the session boundary is unknown.
